facts.statement: Zhenyuanopterus is a boreopterid pterosaur found in the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Zhenyuanopterus is a genus of boreopterid pterosaur which is known from Lower Cretaceous (early Aptian stage) Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The only known species, Zhenyuanopterus longirostris, was first described and named by Lü Junchang.
facts.quote: It contains one species, Zhenyuanopterus longirostris, which was first described and named by Lü Junchang.

facts.statement: Lü Junchang named the species Zhenyuanopterus longirostris in 2005.
facts.quote: Zhenyuanopterus longirostris was named by paleontologist Lü Junchang in 2005.

facts.statement: The genus name honors Sun Zhenyuan, who provided the fossils to Lü Junchang.
facts.quote: The genus is named after Sun Zhenyuan, who gave Lü Junchang the fossils along with Zi Fan.

facts.statement: A single complete skeleton, catalogued as GLGMV 0001, was found at the Huangbanjigou locality and is housed in the Guilin Longshan Geological Museum.
facts.quote: One specimen is known; a complete skeleton, it was found in the Huangbanjigou locality of the Yixian Formation, and it is catalogued as GLGMV 0001 in the Guilin Longshan Geological Museum in Guangxi, China.

facts.statement: Teng Fangfang and colleagues provided a further description of the genus in 2014.
facts.quote: In 2014, Teng Fangfang and colleagues described it.

facts.statement: The skull of the type specimen measures 54.5 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The skull of the type specimen of Zhenyuanopterus measures 54.5 cm long.

facts.statement: The animal possessed a rectangular crest along the snout and a smaller crest at the back of the head.
facts.quote: It possesses a rectangular crest extending along the top of the snout, and another small crest at the back of the head.

facts.statement: The eye socket is shaped like an inverted triangle.
facts.quote: The eye socket is in the shape of an inverted triangle.

facts.statement: The animal had 86 teeth in its upper jaw and 86 in its lower jaw.
facts.quote: There are 86 teeth in the upper and another 86 teeth in the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanopterus had an estimated wingspan of 3.5 to 4 meters, making it one of the larger boreopterids.
facts.quote: Zhenyuanopterus was estimated to have a wingspan of 3.5 to 4 m, making it one of the larger boreopterids.

facts.statement: It is suggested that Zhenyuanopterus foraged by swimming and trapping aquatic prey with its needle-like teeth, a method similar to modern Platanista river dolphins.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that Zhenyuanopterus foraged while swimming, trapping prey within its needle-like teeth, a method similar to that of modern Platanista river dolphins, which display a similar dentition.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Zhenyuanopterus is a distinct species or simply the adult form of the juvenile genus Boreopterus, with differences attributed to age.
facts.quote: However, it has been suggested that this animal is actually the adult of Boreopterus, which is known to be a juvenile; all known specimens of the crestless Boreopterus are smaller than the large, crested Zhenyuanopterus, and most of the differences between them can be explained as age-related.

facts.statement: Zhenyuanopterus lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
